cabin_presets.name: ryanair
cabin_presets.why: the single-class high-density preset, which rewrites economy's geometry

cabin_presets.name: iberia
cabin_presets.why: the three-class preset, which writes four classes and a length mix

cabin_presets.name: emirates
cabin_presets.why: the premium-heavy preset, the only one that fills the first cabin

cabin_presets.name: custom_percent
cabin_presets.why: Custom in percent mode re-solves the counts from the shares on every call rather than returning early

cabin_presets.name: custom_count_already_seated
cabin_presets.why: Custom in count mode with seats already configured is the no-op return the optimizer loop takes on every evaluation

cabin_presets.name: custom_count_empty
cabin_presets.why: Custom in count mode with nothing configured yet floor-fills economy so the cabin is never silently empty

cabin_presets.name: custom_cargo_empty
cabin_presets.why: the freighter side of the same first-time fill: 70% of geometric capacity

cabin_presets.name: max_payload
cabin_presets.why: the freighter preset that fills every position, and forces the four cargo defaults on the way

cabin_presets.name: unknown_preset
cabin_presets.why: a name no branch matches returns without touching anything, which is what keeps a stale saved file from emptying a cabin

geometry.name: a320
geometry.why: a narrowbody: the smallest usable width

geometry.name: a380
geometry.why: the one preset whose height clears 1.15 diameters, so the only one that reaches the double-deck branch

geometry.name: thick_wall
geometry.why: a wall thick enough to drive internal_half_height onto its 0.1 m floor and usable_width onto its zero floor

layouts.name: default_single_class
layouts.why: no class carries a seat count, so classes() is empty and the engine falls back to one economy cabin sized to num_passengers

layouts.name: a320_high_density
layouts.why: a floor-limited narrowbody at the regulatory minimum pitch: the pitch-stretch multiplier stays at 1.0 and the exit cap does not bind

layouts.name: b787_three_class
layouts.why: three classes on one deck, so the inter-class monument bays and the class-boundary handoff are both reached

layouts.name: b787_exit_limited
layouts.why: far more seats requested than CS-25.807 will certify, so the layout truncates on max_certifiable_capacity rather than on floor length

layouts.name: a380_double_deck
layouts.why: two passenger decks: the class index carries across the deck boundary, and each deck gets its own exit set

layouts.name: crowded_monuments
layouts.why: more monuments than bays, so _monument_fill_order cycles and _stack_y narrows the later items instead of overlapping them

layouts.name: belly_freight
layouts.why: an explicit belly load competing with the structural-payload auto-fill, and the hold-capacity clamp above both

layouts.name: belly_overflow
layouts.why: a belly load past what the holds can hold, so the freight is clamped to the capacity the checked bags leave rather than overflowing

layouts.name: bag_overflow
layouts.why: checked baggage alone past the holds' capacity, which is the only way to reach the bulk-overflow guard: the belly freight is clamped to what the bags leave, and the bags themselves are not

layouts.name: no_structural_cap
layouts.why: with no structural cap the belly auto-fill is off entirely, so only the checked bags reach the holds

layouts.name: cargo_target_cg
layouts.why: a freighter with a real operating-empty mass and CG, so the required payload CG is solved backwards from the target aircraft CG

layouts.name: cargo_no_oew
layouts.why: the same freighter with no operating-empty mass supplied, which is the branch every caller that only wants the payload's own CG takes

layouts.name: cargo_door_proximity
layouts.why: the door-proximity priority with all three doors placed explicitly, so none of the three 'or' fallbacks fires

layouts.name: cargo_uniform
layouts.why: the one strategy that spreads the load rather than filling positions in priority order (fill_full=False)

layouts.name: cargo_min_pallets
layouts.why: the fall-through strategy branch, with a target of zero so the 25% MAC default is what the loader trims to

layouts.name: cargo_narrowbody
layouts.why: a narrowbody hold too shallow for an LD3, so the loader degrades through LOWER_HOLD_FALLBACKS to the reduced-height container

layouts.name: cargo_lower_deck_only
layouts.why: no main deck at all, and a coarse trim step, which is the configuration the passenger engine builds its bag loader with

layouts.name: cargo_over_capacity
layouts.why: more payload asked for than there are positions to hold it, so the solver's total-capacity clamp is what decides the load

oew.name: all_zero
oew.why: no mass at all: the divide-by-zero guard

oew.name: negative_component
oew.why: a negative mass is floored at zero rather than subtracting moment

simulations.name: b787_iberia
simulations.why: the shipped three-class long-haul mix, where the premium share drives service_reserve_len hard

simulations.name: b787_emirates
simulations.why: a mix with a first cabin, so all four class branches are reached across this section

simulations.name: a380_iberia
simulations.why: the multi-class mix across two decks, where the per-deck cap rather than the total is what binds

simulations.name: a320_tiny
simulations.why: one very long-pitch class, which is where the last-class 'absorb whatever is left' budget branch shows
